We regularize the problem by restricting the admissible function class through constraints justified by first principles---support on $x\in[0,1]$, endpoint vanishing, unit normalization, and, for the pion, the exact $x\leftrightarrow 1-x$ symmetry---and by complementing these hard constraints with differentiable penalties that suppress the spurious multiple maxima and central concavity changes typical of ill-posed inversions. We parameterize the unknown function with two interchangeable neural cores, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN), and find that the KAN reconstructs the target distributions more accurately, most markedly in the asymmetric (kaon) case. We attribute this advantage to the locality of the B-spline basis underlying the KAN, which localizes corrections during moment matching and damps the global oscillations to which the MLP is prone. Benchmarks against synthetic targets, using both ten and five input moments, support these conclusions.
items.title: Reconstructing Meson Parton Distributions from Mellin Moments with Artificial Neural Networks

items.summary: Phylogenetic networks provide a natural framework for representing reticulate evolutionary events such as horizontal gene transfer and hybridization. In the present manuscript, we investigate the identifiability of phylogenetic networks under (hardwired) parsimony, a natural extension of Maximum Parsimony from trees to networks. More precisely, we ask which structural features of a network can be uniquely inferred from so-called $A_k$-alignments under this criterion. While identifiability has been studied extensively for phylogenetic trees under parsimony, little is known about the identifiability of networks under hardwired parsimony. We take a first step towards addressing this gap by developing a general framework for studying identifiability under hardwired parsimony. We then use this framework to show that the tree of blobs of a phylogenetic network can be reconstructed from its $A_1$-alignment. This result can be viewed as a natural extension of Buneman's well-known splits equivalence theorem. Finally, we show that, under hardwired parsimony, cycles of length at least $5$ cannot in general be uniquely identified from character data, establishing a fundamental limitation of hardwired parsimony.
items.title: An extension of the classic Buneman theorem from phylogenetic trees to networks

items.summary: LUNA is a differentiable astrophysical hydrodynamics code written in JAX, with hand-written Pallas kernels as a fast path on GPUs. It solves the Euler equations in one, two and three dimensions with an unsplit, second-order MUSCL-Hancock scheme and HLLC or HLL Riemann solvers, and runs on CPUs and on many NVIDIA or AMD GPUs, with the domain split over devices. Self-gravity is solved with periodic or isolated boundaries and couples to the gas conserving energy; comoving cosmology evolves gas together with dark-matter particles; radiative cooling, driven turbulence and starburst energy and mass injection are built in. Examples of what it does: shock tubes, blast waves and Kelvin-Helmholtz, Rayleigh-Taylor and Richtmyer-Meshkov instabilities; Jeans collapse and collapsing self-gravitating clouds; the cosmic web of gas and dark matter from cosmological initial conditions; driven supersonic turbulence; galactic winds blown out of a starburst disk; and inverse problems, such as optimising initial conditions with gradients taken through the solver. Non-equilibrium chemistry and cooling networks, radiation transport, sink particles and star formation with stellar dynamics and feedback through Torch/AMUSE, and block-based adaptive mesh refinement are included as experimental modules. Validated capabilities are tested against exact solutions or other codes (AthenaK, Arepo, RAMSES), whose reference solutions are published with the code.
items.title: LUNA: A Differentiable Astrophysical Hydrodynamics Code

items.summary: This paper is concerned with an inverse source problem for the stochastic fractional Helmholtz equation in a three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is modeled as real Gaussian spatial white noise with an unknown nonnegative strength function. For admissible frequencies, we establish well-posedness of the radiating solution in the distributional sense and show that it has a smooth representation outside the source region. For the inverse problem, by using two-point correlations of the field measured in an exterior open set at a single frequency, we prove a logarithmic stability estimate for recovering the source strength under an a priori Sobolev bound. As a uniform Hölder stability estimate is unavailable for the general admissible class, by assuming the difference between two source strengths has a fixed sign, we improve the stability to Hölder continuity with an optimal Hölder exponent. The analysis combines scattering theory and quantitative continuation for the fractional Laplacian using the Caffarelli-Silvestre extension.
items.title: Inverse source problem for the stochastic fractional Helmholtz equation in inhomogeneous media

items.summary: Flow models have recently emerged as powerful generative priors for solving inverse problems. Despite their success, most existing flow-based inverse problem solvers initialize the reconstruction process with random Gaussian noise. However, recent studies in image generation have shown that the choice of initial noise can significantly influence generation outcomes. The role of initialization as a distinct design choice in flow-based inverse problem solving remains comparatively underexplored. In this work, we systematically evaluate noise initialization strategies while holding the downstream flow-based inverse solver fixed. We propose Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion (RA-DGI), a method that constructs improved initial noise by leveraging retrieved proxy clean images and dual-guided inversion. Extensive experiments across multiple inverse problems demonstrate that the quality of the initial noise substantially affects reconstruction fidelity and perceptual performance. RA-DGI outperforms standard random initialization and achieves superior results compared to inference-time scaling strategies, while requiring less computational overhead. These findings highlight initialization as a critical yet previously overlooked factor in flow-based inverse problem solvers.
items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion for Flow-Based Inverse Problem Solvers

items.summary: Rumor models of the Daley--Kendall and Maki--Thompson family anchor the statistical mechanics of social contagion, yet the stifler composition a rumor leaves behind has resisted closed-form analysis. Inspired by the asymmetric two-step pairing (A2SP) process of step-growth polymerization, we import its common-factor cancellation into a minimal two-stage MT variant in which re-contacted spreaders are re-activated into a senior class at rate $αk_1$ rather than stifled, and obtain exact terminal-state theorems. (i) Saturation: the rumor exhausts the ignorant pool for every stifling-to-recruitment ratio $μ>0$, with a three-way tail classification and a logarithmically critical line at $μ=1$. (ii) Final size: the terminal stifler pool splits as $(x_1,x_2)=(μ/(α+μ),α/(α+μ))$, independent of seed size; the fingerprint inverts linearly ($α=μx_2/x_1$) and matches Gillespie simulations within $0.95\%$. (iii) Pooled versus history-resolved: pooled statistics are exactly $α$-free on any static graph; only the history-resolved composition carries $α$. Restoring the classic teller-retires channel breaks the exact closure beyond quantified gates (contact rates of $1$--$3\%$ of $k_1$ for spreader channels at $μ\leq1.5$, up to $32\%$ at $μ=2$), and on configuration-model networks the composition bias decays as $\langle k\rangle^{-0.71}$. An exploratory inversion of 354,930 Higgs--Twitter retweet episodes, screened by an identity check and four negative controls, yields $\hatα=2.21\%$ (joint cluster-bootstrap CI $[1.6\%,3.0\%]$; $\approx3.7\%$ after calibration at the matched threshold). items.title: Terminal-state theorems for a two-stage Maki--Thompson rumor model: final size, stifler composition, and non-identifiability from pooled statistics

items.summary: As a paradigm for describing open-quantum-system dynamics, the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation generally modifies state norms, complicating coherent control over the system's Hilbert space. With a general instantaneous frame spanned by biorthogonal ancillary bases, we develop a biorthogonal quantum-control theory for discrete-variable systems governed by time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. In particular, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for extracting the transitionless pathways that transport parallel in ket and bra states. When this condition is satisfied by a set of projectors constructed with biorthogonal basis states, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian becomes diagonal in the relevant biorthogonal subspace, enabling arbitrary initial state to evolve as a superposition of controlled transitionless passages. We further identify the parametric constraints under which the transformation linking the initial and final states becomes unitary. As a result, the final system state is automatically normalized even though the transitional dynamics is nonunitary. Our theory is justified by the bidirectional population transfer and a holomonic quantum gate implemented by a non-Hermitian three-level system in $Λ$ type. For the population transfer, controlled gain and loss reduce the required coherent pulse area, enabling shorter transfer times than the Hermitian benchmark with the same average Rabi frequency. Our work integrates the universal quantum control (UQC) into the biorthogonal representation, displaying full-rank passage engineering with coherent operations in non-Hermitian systems.
items.title: Biorthogonal universal quantum control

items.summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has become a standard reasoning strategy in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), showing strong performance in complex vision-language tasks such as reasoning segmentation. However, our analysis reveals that indiscriminate CoT usage can lead to degraded performance by inducing unnecessary reasoning, a phenomenon we term overthinking. In reasoning segmentation, overthinking often leads to misalignment between the query's intent and visual grounding. To address this, we propose Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought (DA-CoT), a training-free adaptive framework that selectively triggers CoT based on the input's intrinsic difficulty. We find that the entropy of the model's attention maps reliably reflects task difficulty: low entropy indicates confident, localized grounding, while high entropy suggests uncertainty and potential benefit from CoT. DA-CoT uses this entropy signal to determine whether to apply CoT prompting. Additionally, we introduce a Bidirectional Rethinking mechanism that enables the model to automatically flip its reasoning decision when the initial output fails, enhancing robustness by recovering from failures induced by overthinking and underthinking. DA-CoT demonstrates its effectiveness by achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Reasoning Segmentation benchmarks while significantly improving inference efficiency.
items.title: Attention Maps Know When to Think: Training-Free Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Segmentation

items.summary: Reproducibility data and code supporting the study “Parameter fragility in the reanalysis of published Mössbauer spectra” by Osman Armağan and Muhammed Emin Bedir. The release contains retained spectral coordinates, 44 primary archive fits and their start records, 44,000 archive perturbation refits, 24,000 paired-study refits for 12 panels from five publications, model configurations, 33 implementation-check records, 477 saved field-profile trials, provenance and source tables, bibliographic records, plotting programs, and a self-contained analysis notebook. Default execution verifies retained results and reconstructs figures without optimization; optional reruns write separate outputs. The archive contains 44 spectra from 19 publications (eight connected coauthor groups). Paired numerical references are author-supplied plotted spectra, not verified instrument-level raw counts. The analysis describes parameter sensitivity and agreement with published fits, not physical-accuracy guarantees. No independent external magnetic validation or second-operator extraction is included. Download and extract Zenodo_Upload_Files.zip. It contains five files: Reproducibility_Package.zip (complete data/code release and integrity manifest), Reproduce_Analysis.ipynb (standalone notebook), Figures_600dpi.zip (12 main/supplementary figures in PNG, TIFF, PDF and SVG), README.txt, and CITATION.cff. Extract Reproducibility_Package.zip for direct access to individual data/code files. For notebook use, follow README.txt and select the inner Reproducibility_Package.zip when prompted. Author-created material is distributed under CC BY 4.0. Third-party software and source data retain their original terms and attribution; no additional third-party rights are granted. Article PDFs are not redistributed. This is a separate release from the authors’ earlier provenance/ML corpus (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21997560; related article DOI 10.1039/d6ra08367f).
items.title: Parameter fragility in the reanalysis of published Mössbauer spectra: Reproducibility data and code

items.summary: The July 2026 counterexample settled the Jacobian conjecture in dimensions N ≥ 3 and left JC(2) as the open case. This paper develops an exact-arithmetic program on the planar case. The Keller condition J(P, Q) = 1 is linear in Q for fixed P; the resulting machine (eliminate, parametrize the consistency variety, complete, invert) closes the columns min deg ≤ 2 uniformly (one closed inverse for the whole quasi-triangular class), forces perfect-power tops at bidegrees (2, n) and (3, n), and inverts every consistent stratum it has met. Four unconditional exclusion theorems follow from a weight-class calculus: a two-term P = x + a x^u y^v is never a Keller component at any partner degree; neither is any lower-weight perturbation of it; no Keller component carries a Newton top edge anchored at the linear vertex x with interior direction; and if x is a vertex of the Newton polygon then P = x + f(y) exactly (the vertex dichotomy). The residual open core is the transport of the Keller constant along the staircase of Newton vertices swallowing x: we show the completion window is block-triangular under the edge grading, exhibit the classwise transport chain as an executable elimination whose obstruction always localizes at the constant's class, and prove the corresponding fifth exclusion: for primitive tops the certificate-tower induction closes it unconditionally at all partner degrees (cleared base certificates with monomial pairings such as -13860 a^7, plus a resonance-reduction lemma showing window growth can never repair the constant's row). A recalibration against the primary sources shows that our composite-gcd certificates replicate literature-covered territory (the verified floor is gcd ≤ 8, primes, 2p, then Heitmann's B ≥ 16 and the Guccione-Guccione-Valqui dichotomy B = 16 or B > 20), and that the open frontier is the B = 16 normal form together with the single surviving degree pair (72, 108) below 125. items.summary: We study the critical Sobolev-curl quotient on $\mathbb{R}^3$ at the conformally invariant exponent $p=3/2$. Its sharp constant and optimizers were posed as open problems in the literature. We identify the toroidal and poloidal extremals. Two structural facts are used. First, the critical curl--curl equation is self-dual: the map $u\mapsto|\nabla\times u|^{-1/2}\nabla\times u$ is an involution on finite-energy solutions. It is the self-dual case of a duality between the exponents $p$ and $3p/(4p-3)$, which exchanges toroidal and poloidal fields and relates the sharp constants. Second, the toroidal minimization problem reduces exactly to a subcritical $3/2$-Laplace problem on the hyperbolic plane. Combined with symmetry and shooting results, these facts show that the two restricted sharp constants coincide. They also classify the gauge-minimal extremals: these are unique up to scaling and the Euclidean transformations realizing hyperbolic isometries, semi-explicit, and dual to each other. For nonzero one-signed profiles radial about a fixed hyperbolic centre, a gauge-canonical inverse of the duality yields an iteration by one-dimensional quadratures: the quotients are nonincreasing and converge to the restricted sharp constant, while the normalized iterates converge to the extremal pair. The first step from an explicit competitor gives the new upper bound $96\sqrt{15}π/(5\sqrt{4455π-13568})\approx11.2948$ for the restricted constants. The unrestricted sharp constant remains open. As an application, bounded axisymmetric poloidal potentials admit no $L^2$ zero mode of the Weyl-Dirac operator. items.summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has become a standard reasoning strategy in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), showing strong performance in complex vision-language tasks such as reasoning segmentation. However, our analysis reveals that indiscriminate CoT usage can lead to degraded performance by inducing unnecessary reasoning, a phenomenon we term overthinking. In reasoning segmentation, overthinking often leads to misalignment between the query's intent and visual grounding. To address this, we propose Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought (DA-CoT), a training-free adaptive framework that selectively triggers CoT based on the input's intrinsic difficulty. We find that the entropy of the model's attention maps reliably reflects task difficulty: low entropy indicates confident, localized grounding, while high entropy suggests uncertainty and potential benefit from CoT. DA-CoT uses this entropy signal to determine whether to apply CoT prompting. Additionally, we introduce a Bidirectional Rethinking mechanism that enables the model to automatically flip its reasoning decision when the initial output fails, enhancing robustness by recovering from failures induced by overthinking and underthinking. DA-CoT demonstrates its effectiveness by achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Reasoning Segmentation benchmarks while significantly improving inference efficiency.
items.title: Attention Maps Know When to Think: Training-Free Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Segmentation

items.summary: Iterative language-model optimizers refine prompts and programs by evaluating a candidate, showing a proposer model a sample of failing cases, and keeping revisions that improve performance. Recent work attributes the limits of this loop to narrow single-round reflection, introducing full-set error clustering, targeted minibatches, or larger proposer models so the optimizer sees more failure modes per step. Yet every existing evaluation tests these mechanisms exclusively inside lineage-preserving search, where each revision edits a surviving parent, leaving the contribution of parent inheritance confounded with the breadth of per-round feedback. Across 1,750 pre-registered runs spanning nine prompt and program synthesis benchmarks, we separate parent inheritance from feedback disclosure under matched evaluation budgets. We find that greedy parent inheritance drives the vast majority of optimization progress, outperforming seed-reset resampling even when seed-reset proposals receive a clustered summary of all failures in every round or use a larger proposer model. While full-set error clustering and diverse failure selection improve single-step rewrites from the seed and accelerate the opening rounds of search, sequential parent inheritance rapidly closes this gap as solved error modes are retained in the candidate and filtered from subsequent failure lists. Moreover, decomposing token expenditure in GEPA reveals that proposer reflection accounts for only a small fraction of total cost whereas validation and minibatch gating consume nearly the entire budget, showing that greedy parent inheritance over raw failures captures the gains of complex reflective loops at a fraction of their compute.
items.title: Lineage Is Memory: Parent Inheritance and Feedback Disclosure in Short-Budget LLM-Guided Optimization

items.summary: Flapping-wing simulation must reconcile high-frequency wingbeat aerodynamics with the slower dynamics relevant to flight control and reinforcement learning. We present FlapSim, a modular open-source MuJoCo simulation platform that combines robot descriptions, wing geometry, and composable aerodynamic models in a deterministic simulation pipeline. Across $48$ held-out scenarios spanning frequency, gimbal, wind, frequency-step, gust, and cross-robot flat-plate regimes, we compare five reduced-order configurations operating at $1\,\text{ms}$ with a $50\,μ\text{s}$ quasi-steady blade-element reference. The built-in hover cycle-averaged baseline achieves a $67.51\times$ CPU speedup but only $0.6593$ mean wrench fidelity. Combining multirate $21$-substep clock synchronization, three-dimensional linear/quadratic inflow and gust coupling, analytical blade-element geometry scaling, and phase-locked $1f\text{--}6f$ harmonics raises mean fidelity to $0.9646$ at a $65.19\times$ speedup in a five-block model. A streamlined four-block model without explicit step-transient lag states achieves $0.9662$ fidelity at a $67.98\times$ speedup. Controlled ablations show that stroke harmonics are particularly important during frequency transitions, improving held-out frequency-step fidelity by $+0.3176$. Transfer-function analysis explains this effect: fixed-window cycle averaging retains harmonic contributions when the wingbeat frequency changes, so within-cycle reconstruction also improves the filtered wrench. Once phase alignment and harmonic synthesis are included, explicit transient lag states provide no additional benefit in this benchmark. These results characterize the accuracy--computation tradeoff of the aerodynamic hierarchy and identify timing, inflow, geometry, and harmonic representation as central considerations for reduced-order flapping-wing simulation.
items.title: FlapSim: A Composable MuJoCo Simulation Platform and Reduced-Order Aerodynamic Model Hierarchy for Flapping-Wing Robotics

items.summary: As a paradigm for describing open-quantum-system dynamics, the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation generally modifies state norms, complicating coherent control over the system's Hilbert space. With a general instantaneous frame spanned by biorthogonal ancillary bases, we develop a biorthogonal quantum-control theory for discrete-variable systems governed by time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. In particular, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for extracting the transitionless pathways that transport parallel in ket and bra states. When this condition is satisfied by a set of projectors constructed with biorthogonal basis states, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian becomes diagonal in the relevant biorthogonal subspace, enabling arbitrary initial state to evolve as a superposition of controlled transitionless passages. We further identify the parametric constraints under which the transformation linking the initial and final states becomes unitary. As a result, the final system state is automatically normalized even though the transitional dynamics is nonunitary. Our theory is justified by the bidirectional population transfer and a holomonic quantum gate implemented by a non-Hermitian three-level system in $Λ$ type. For the population transfer, controlled gain and loss reduce the required coherent pulse area, enabling shorter transfer times than the Hermitian benchmark with the same average Rabi frequency. Our work integrates the universal quantum control (UQC) into the biorthogonal representation, displaying full-rank passage engineering with coherent operations in non-Hermitian systems.
items.title: Biorthogonal universal quantum control

items.summary: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. However, several models exhibit highly asymmetric authorisation behaviour, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarifiable ASK cases and a strong preference for BLOCK. This motivates safety sufficiency: whether a predictive interface preserves and exposes the policy-decisive information required to distinguish actions that may be EXECUTED, require clarification through ASK, or should be BLOCKED. We introduce SafeWebWorld, a benchmark for evaluating safety sufficiency across five web-safety domains through action-conditioned futures, policy-decisive evidence, and policy-conditioned decisions. Under a controlled Security-Aligned Supervised Fine-Tuning protocol, evidence preservation can improve substantially while authorisation-sensitive decisions deteriorate. To determine whether this deterioration reflects loss of authorisation-sensitive score structure or a failure of the decision readout, we introduce Latent Authorisation Recovery (LAR). Frozen-score recalibration reveals substantial but backbone-dependent recovery, while paired recovery provides only a modest additional gain. Yet within-family and matched-authorisation evaluations remain poor, showing that aggregate recoverability does not imply robust fine-grained authorisation behaviour. Overall, plausible prediction, evidence preservation, and aggregate recovery are each insufficient on their own to establish robust authorisation.
items.title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models

items.summary: In text-to-SQL and AI-agent analytics, successful SQL execution does not establish semantic correctness under changing business definitions. We study revalidation of fixed queries after changes to refund attribution, tax treatment, eligible populations and exchange-rate dates. An executable verification profile binds the requested revision and knowledge cutoff to legal counterexample data and exact monetary comparison. A preregistered confirmation on 32 newly authored revision families and two local producer bundles retains 192 query-definition cells: 144 nonconforming, 36 finite-suite agreeing and 12 unresolved. Of the nonconforming cells, 63 agree on the current snapshot. At an eight-ledger budget, obligation-guided checking detects 137 discrepancies versus 127 for generic ordering, a paired difference of 6.9 percentage points (family bootstrap 95% interval [2.1, 13.6]; exact family sign-flip p=0.0156). Every ledger arm rejects zero of the 36 agreeing cells. Current-obligation and equal-weight scoring match the guided result, identifying coverage rather than revision-specific priority as the observed source of benefit. Controlled assays, a natural-query pilot and repeated samples provide separate mechanism and robustness evidence. A legal discrepancy refutes conformance; agreement remains restricted to the recorded suite. The study establishes an auditable business-semantic revalidation profile within its authored schema and local-model scope.
items.title: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics

items.summary: Rumor models of the Daley--Kendall and Maki--Thompson family anchor the statistical mechanics of social contagion, yet the stifler composition a rumor leaves behind has resisted closed-form analysis. Inspired by the asymmetric two-step pairing (A2SP) process of step-growth polymerization, we import its common-factor cancellation into a minimal two-stage MT variant in which re-contacted spreaders are re-activated into a senior class at rate $αk_1$ rather than stifled, and obtain exact terminal-state theorems. (i) Saturation: the rumor exhausts the ignorant pool for every stifling-to-recruitment ratio $μ>0$, with a three-way tail classification and a logarithmically critical line at $μ=1$. (ii) Final size: the terminal stifler pool splits as $(x_1,x_2)=(μ/(α+μ),α/(α+μ))$, independent of seed size; the fingerprint inverts linearly ($α=μx_2/x_1$) and matches Gillespie simulations within $0.95\%$. (iii) Pooled versus history-resolved: pooled statistics are exactly $α$-free on any static graph; only the history-resolved composition carries $α$. Restoring the classic teller-retires channel breaks the exact closure beyond quantified gates (contact rates of $1$--$3\%$ of $k_1$ for spreader channels at $μ\leq1.5$, up to $32\%$ at $μ=2$), and on configuration-model networks the composition bias decays as $\langle k\rangle^{-0.71}$. An exploratory inversion of 354,930 Higgs--Twitter retweet episodes, screened by an identity check and four negative controls, yields $\hatα=2.21\%$ (joint cluster-bootstrap CI $[1.6\%,3.0\%]$; $\approx3.7\%$ after calibration at the matched threshold). Terminal compositions identify this effective re-activation rate, an upper bound on contact-coupled re-activation; the mechanism itself requires timing information beyond the terminal state.
items.title: Terminal-state theorems for a two-stage Maki--Thompson rumor model: final size, stifler composition, and non-identifiability from pooled statistics

items.summary: We address the inverse problem of reconstructing a meson parton distribution function (PDF) or parton distribution amplitude (PDA) at a fixed scale from a finite set of Mellin moments. At finite moment order this map is ill posed in the Hadamard sense: the moments do not determine a unique, stable pointwise $x$-dependence, and small data perturbations can produce large changes in the reconstruction. We regularize the problem by restricting the admissible function class through constraints justified by first principles---support on $x\in[0,1]$, endpoint vanishing, unit normalization, and, for the pion, the exact $x\leftrightarrow 1-x$ symmetry---and by complementing these hard constraints with differentiable penalties that suppress the spurious multiple maxima and central concavity changes typical of ill-posed inversions. We parameterize the unknown function with two interchangeable neural cores, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN), and find that the KAN reconstructs the target distributions more accurately, most markedly in the asymmetric (kaon) case. We attribute this advantage to the locality of the B-spline basis underlying the KAN, which localizes corrections during moment matching and damps the global oscillations to which the MLP is prone. Benchmarks against synthetic targets, using both ten and five input moments, support these conclusions.
items.title: Reconstructing Meson Parton Distributions from Mellin Moments with Artificial Neural Networks

items.summary: Multi-turn negotiation remains a challenging problem for large language model (LLM) agents. While LLMs can conduct natural-language dialogue, existing benchmarks predominantly assess only agreement rates, overlooking whether negotiated commitments actually create value once executed. To address this gap, we introduce TradeWar, a multi-country simulation benchmark that translates negotiation dialogues into concrete tariff and trade-share policies, enforces capacity and network constraints during settlement, and evaluates outcomes via an Economic Health Index (EHI). To solve this execution-grounded task, we propose TACTIC (Trade-aware Adaptive Consolidation and Theory-of-mind for International Commerce), an agent that iteratively refines its negotiation strategy across episodes-without updating base LLM weights-by leveraging prior experience, opponent behavior, and past settlement outcomes. Despite using zero-shot chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, PromptLLM attains a 75% agreement rate but only 57.1 final EHI (*100), whereas TACTIC reaches 68.8. Across 20 sequential episodes and three seeds, TACTIC's final EHI improves from 58.2 to 73.2, compared with 65.2 for an ablation without cross-episode updates. Under technology-controls and energy-crisis shocks, TACTIC also exhibits smaller performance degradation than PromptLLM and MemoryLLM. These results indicate that CoT deliberation and interaction memory alone do not fully address delayed execution feedback, whereas settlement-grounded adaptation improves long-horizon negotiation in TradeWar.
items.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents

items.summary: Flagship 60/60 Can distributed research stations preserve qualified biosafe work and genuine operator exit when suppliers, control versions or core services disappear? TRUSTWORTHY AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC MANUFACTURING PLATFORMS FOR REGENERATIVE MEDICINE AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Nano Regenerative Biomanufacturing series investigates bounded autonomous manufacturing under explicit authorization and independent release. Its scientific coupling is nanorobotics x autonomous biomanufacturing x regenerative quality governance. The evidence perimeter is prospective and nonclinical, using closed in-vitro systems, organ-on-chip platforms or authorized ex-vivo material; neither clinical efficacy nor autonomous human intervention is claimed. The falsifiable question is: Can distributed research stations preserve qualified biosafe work and genuine operator exit when suppliers, control versions or core services disappear? The proposed minimum demonstration is: Two independent community laboratories reconstruct and release nonclinical mock devices from a shared open evidence package. Strong comparators include centralized controlled manufacture, skilled manual labs and single-vendor automation. The central competing explanation is distributed autonomy secretly dependent on centralized reagents, controls or calibration. The noncompensatory stop rule is: operator exit becomes impossible, site performance gap grows or minimum safe service is interrupted. Every eligible, stopped, refused and unsuccessful experiment belongs to the full denominator. Thirty conditional mathematical plates specify different analytic roles, measurements, units and blind failure tests. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 individual research investigations. Two hundred Research Gates organize twenty causal challenge families across ten primary physical observables, each with an independently read companion, concealed intervention, matched comparator, explicit rival and refusal gate. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future experimental and evidence instruments. All are experimental plans rather than executed observations. The source Atlas and methodology ancestors provide reference architecture but do not establish the new integrated candidate. Source-supplied ancestry includes 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020; source-associated external DOI candidates must be bibliographically checked before citation. Research Gate lexical differentiation is not proof of scientific originality. The PDF is English-only and a separate QA record states outstanding independent physics, biology and DOI verification.
